subject: Clarify dedicated pool queueing behavior + mitigation plan (HelioHealth)
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@heliohealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@heliohealth.com
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected tail latency on dedicated pool — need queueing behavior clarified

Hi Marissa,

We ran a 48-hour soak on the dedicated GPU pool you provisioned for HelioHealth (250 reserved vGPU units) and observed several 95/99th tail latency spikes during peak windows. The average token throughput matches the commitment in the SLO doc, but the tail latency occasionally jumps to 1.8–2.2s per token for short bursts, which is outside what our product team expects for latency-sensitive inference.

Can you confirm:
- How Redwood prioritizes requests across reserved vs. burst capacity when pool utilization is near 100%?
- Whether there are queueing tiers (e.g., tail-priority) or backpressure rules we should be aware of?

This is urgent for our go-live on Oct 10. We need a concrete mitigation plan and whether any SLA credit/compensation will be offered if tail latency exceeds the agreed target during our acceptance tests. Attaching the trace we captured.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Turner
Senior Platform Engineer, HelioHealth
attachments: queueing_trace_20260928.zip (pcap + traces)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected tail latency on dedicated pool — need queueing behavior clarified

Alex — thanks for the trace and the clear summary. I’m copying our infra and CS leads so we can triage quickly. Quick answers up front:
- Reserved capacity is served from the dedicated pool first; burst capacity is only used when reserved is exhausted, but there are internal short-term dequeue windows we apply to protect latency SLOs.
- There are two queueing tiers: reserved-priority and best-effort (burst). However, tail behavior depends on request size mix and KV cache eviction patterns.

We’ll investigate the exact cause of the 95/99 spikes and propose mitigations (config changes + temporary routing policy) by EOD tomorrow. We’ll also outline a remediation credit framework if the bursts are due to a platform-side scheduling issue.

Action items: 
- Jonas: run the trace analysis and surface queueing events.
- Laura: prepare a customer-facing mitigation and credit proposal.
- Soojin: hold 20% of Oct committed capacity in reserve for HelioHealth until we sign off on the mitigation plan.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

On Mon, Sep 28, 2026 at 1:05 PM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Alex — thanks for the trace and the clear summary. I’m copying our infra and CS leads so we can triage quickly.

Alex, I pulled the attached pcap and the request-level logs correlated to the pool. Preliminary findings:
- During the spikes, the CUDA occupancy for one node dropped briefly because of a KV cache eviction sweep triggered by a single long-context job. That caused ~70ms per-request spikes on that node; the scheduler then routed subsequent requests to remaining nodes, increasing queueing across the pool.
- The dedicated pool does enforce reserved-priority, but when a hot KV eviction cascades it can create a localized stall; our default fallback then begins draining best-effort queues into reserved slots to preserve throughput, which raises cross-request tail latency for a short window.

Mitigations I recommend (can be applied today as config flips):
1) Reduce KV sweep aggressiveness for HelioHealth’s pool (temporary patch).
2) Increase soft concurrency limit on reserved nodes from 40→48 to spread load slightly and reduce per-node queue build-up.
3) Apply a short, explicit routing policy for the next 72 hours that pins HelioHealth’s burst requests to a separate set of nodes to avoid cross-traffic.

If we apply 1–3 we should see 95/99s return to target within 1–2 hours of rollout. I’ll schedule the change set for 11:00 PT today pending approvals.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Unexpected tail latency on dedicated pool — need queueing behavior clarified

Thanks Jonas — sounds actionable. Alex, from a commercial standpoint I proposed holding 20% additional reserved capacity for HelioHealth as Marissa mentioned. Two options to make you whole during this acceptance window:
- Option A (temporary credit): If tail latency breaches the agreed SLO during acceptance through Oct 12, Redwood provides a pro-rated usage credit capped at one week of committed fees.
- Option B (SLA amendment): Add a temporary carveout clause for Oct acceptance that enumerates the routing policy changes and gives HelioHealth the right to one free rollback and two weeks of discounted burst usage if platform-side scheduling causes breaches.

If you prefer Option B we’ll route legal to draft the short amendment; Option A can be applied immediately without paperwork. We should decide by EOD to avoid billing surprises.

—Soojin

Subject: Re: Unexpected tail latency on dedicated pool — need queueing behavior clarified

Alex — quick summary and next steps after the soak and mitigations: 
- Jonas applied mitigations (KV sweep dial-down, soft concurrency 40→48, routing pin) on Sep 29 at 11:05 PT. Observed 95/99 latency returned to within targets during the Oct 1–2 soak.
- The concurrency bump is transient and covered by the reserved commitment; there’s no additional charge while we’re in this acceptance window.
- The KV sweep change is a tuning reduction (less aggressive eviction). It may slightly reduce cache freshness in rare long-tail contexts but did not impact model outputs in HelioHealth’s acceptance tests. We will revert to normal sweep aggressiveness after the Oct 10 go-live if you prefer.

Per Soojin’s option: we’ll apply Option A (pro-rated one-week credit cap) automatically if any SLO breach is observed during acceptance through Oct 12. Laura is prepping the credit note and customer communication.

Next steps:
1) Laura to send the formal credit note and acceptance checklist (today).
